Inscript [Fiscal and Economic Sense] Case Study: Kumar’s Blueprint for Financial Freedom Background & Current State: Kumar (Age 25) recently graduated with a postgraduate degree and secured a job in Bengaluru with a fixed salary of ₹24,00,000 per annum. His take-home pay is ₹1,50,000 per month. Liabilities & Cash Flow Dilemma: To fund his education, Kumar took a student loan of ₹20 Lakhs. His monthly EMI for this loan is ₹35,000. To celebrate his new job, his friends are pressuring him to purchase a luxury car worth ₹15 Lakhs on a 5-year loan. Kumar is trying to map out his cash flow to see if he can comfortably manage both EMIs while building his wealth. Future Planning & Asset Allocation: Kumar wants to start building his own investment portfolio. He is deciding whether to put his monthly surplus into 8.05% Taxable RBI Bonds or diversify into Equity Mutual Funds. He is also aware that long-term inflation in India hovers around 7%. Furthermore, his bank account currently holds just ₹1,00,000, and he wants to build a proper safety net before aggressively investing. Investment Returns & Real Estate: Kumar recently analyzed an old family real estate transaction: his father bought a plot of land for ₹1 Crore and sold it exactly 5 years later, netting ₹1.48 Crore after expenses. His father boasts about a massive '48% return.' Looking ahead in his own 30-year blueprint, Kumar plans to eventually acquire three residential properties: his primary residence in Bengaluru, a second home in his native place of Coimbatore, and a third property to keep entirely vacant and locked as a pure long-term investment. Question : Briefly identify the five major heads of income under the Indian Income Tax Act. For Kumar's proposed real estate portfolio, comprising two self-occupied homes and a third kept strictly vacant, determine the applicable income head and explain the specific tax treatment for that third property. (Answer in 100 words, 3 marks) Max Word Count : 100 Min Word Count : 0 Highlight min word : Yes Single Line Response : No Number of Rows : 10 Number Of Columns : 70

[10 Cs of Teamwork] As part of a Software Engineering course team project, a group of students is developing a Community Services Platform. The platform includes modules for membership management, event organization, resource booking, volunteer scheduling, issue tracking, and communication. The leaders of two different teams adopt different working styles: 1. Shipra, the project lead, brings the team together during the initial planning phase to converge and agree on the system requirements and project scope. She then divides the work into modules, assigns each member specific responsibilities and deadlines, and expects them to work independently. She uses weekly progress meetings to check whether each module is progressing according to the plan and whether the outputs fit together. 2. Gaurang, the team lead, involves the team members regularly discussing design ideas, brainstorming solutions for workflow challenges, reviewing each other's work, and jointly refine features such as event management and resource booking. When problems arise, they work together to find and improve solutions and the lead facilitates the team towards a common goal. [10 Cs of Teamwork] What best describes the difference between the two approaches?
options: The first approach emphasizes coordination, while the second emphasizes collaboration
The first approach emphasizes collaboration, while the second emphasizes coordination
questions.correct_answer: The first approach emphasizes coordination, while the second emphasizes collaboration
